exposure: laparoscopic sacral colpopexy with concomitant supracervical hysterectomy (LSCP/SCH)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 136 patients with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse who underwent either laparoscopic sacral hysteropexy or laparoscopic sacral colpopexy with concomitant supracervical hysterectomy.
finding: Both laparoscopic sacral hysteropexy (LSHP) and laparoscopic sacral colpopexy with supracervical hysterectomy (LSCP/SCH) are safe and effective treatments for pelvic organ prolapse, showing similar anatomical and subjective success rates, although LSHP had a significantly shorter operative time.
